avoidable_by: checking data/corpus/<book>/spell/ resolution up front, not only the upstream .lst citation
cause: 6 of 904 candidates (e.g. advanced_players_guide:spell:fester) are pre-.lst-pipeline records sourced web_second_source with no raw_tokens in data/corpus at all, so the evaluator correctly reported them unresolved even though work-inventory.json states a real upstream .lst citation for them
summary: SD31-E6-F2-006: spell caster-level-duration fixture generator corrected 904->898 entries after finding 6 unresolvable against the Rust evaluator's real read path
what: First fixture-generator pass emitted 904 spell_entries citing every DURATION-token-matching held unit's upstream .lst line, without checking whether data/corpus/<book>/spell/*.json (what the Rust evaluator actually reads) carries raw_tokens at all

detected_by: ps -p <pid> -o ppid,cmd showing a second live process tree under the same CARGO_TARGET_DIR after the second launch, cross-checked against /proc/<pid>/environ
impact: Misread mid-stream 'FAIL root-full' output as the whole verify.sh run having finished/failed and relaunched a second ./scripts/verify.sh while the first was still legitimately running through its remaining stages, producing two concurrent verify.sh processes sharing the same CARGO_TARGET_DIR for several minutes
resolution: Killed both process trees cleanly by exact PID (verified CARGO_TARGET_DIR ownership via /proc/<pid>/environ first, per shared-tree discipline), then did one single clean relaunch and waited for the real VERIFY_EXIT= line rather than reacting to an interim per-stage FAIL
summary: SD31-E6-F2-006: verify.sh runs every stage to completion even after an earlier stage fails; reacting to a mid-log FAIL line instead of the final VERIFY_EXIT= caused a redundant concurrent relaunch
